chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥamzah and al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Muyassir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"Shall I not describe to you the wudu of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله?"

Then he took a handful of water and poured it over his face. Then he took a handful and poured it over his arm. Then he took another handful and poured it over his other arm. Then he wiped his head and his feet.
Then he placed his hand on the top of the foot and said, "This is the ankle." He said: and he pointed with his hand to below the heel, then said, "Indeed this is the zhunbub."

key_terms.الْعُرْقُوبِ: the heel tendon/heel area, distinguished from the ankle in the narration
key_terms.ذِرَاعِهِ: his arm, the limb washed in wudu
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, which is wiped in wudu
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, whose practice is being demonstrated
key_terms.قَدَمَيْهِ: his two feet, which are wiped in this narration
key_terms.مَسَحَ: he wiped, referring to the prescribed wiping rather than washing
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being described

ai.seo_question: How is the wudu of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله described in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the wudu of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as demonstrated by Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام. It outlines washing the face and arms with separate handfuls of water, then wiping the head and feet, and it clarifies the location of the ankle relevant to the ruling of wiping the feet in wudu.
